biography.plain_text: Robert E. Riordan was an American magazine publisher and former Newsweek circulation director. As Family Media's controlling shareholder, he acquired and revived Ladies' Home Journal before selling it to Meredith, generating a substantial personal entitlement to the proceeds. He and his wife, Mary Anne, lived in New York and Florida.

long_biography.plain_text:
Magazine publisher Robert Riordan paid close attention to how readers bought and renewed their subscriptions. At Ladies' Home Journal, he raised subscription prices gradually while offering existing readers the chance to renew before an increase. Temporary reductions in newsstand prices were intended to introduce the magazine to new readers.

Riordan also preserved the advertising and editorial budgets inherited from the previous owner. His company bought research on who read and remembered the magazine, giving its advertising sales team more information about the audience. Editor Myrna Blyth continued to lead the editorial operation, while Riordan's contribution centred on circulation and commercial management.
